title: Shape skeletons v1 - one file per skeleton under content/video_engine/effects/skeletons/<id>.json (P66 T1)
description: A skeleton is a DATA file: the approved shape of one beat written as a TEMPLATE of the kit's row grammar (authoring/table.py:1-16 - a row is the tuple (start, end, plate_id, ken_burns, [docks], exit[, species[, camera]])) with named holes the build fills from its AUTHORED beat plan; a NEW skeleton is added by writing a file plus its `source` cite in an approved table, with no code change (P66 T1), which is how P65's promotions widen the library.

act.description: the 11 sentence acts as docs/content-video-engine/SPECIES-BY-SENTENCE.md spells them (section 0 at a glance, section 1 rows 1-10, section 2 row 11 BREAKS); the same 11 as effect_card.schema.json `serves` and effect_recipe.schema.json `acts`

signature.title: the ONE word M46 counts for this skeleton - the move a viewer would name
signature.description: THE CHOREOGRAPHY VOCABULARY, REBUILT FROM THE RECORD (E99 s70 Apply 2, 2026-09-17; the operator: "you completely dropped all of the choreography that gave life to our shorts, you dropped most of the continuity building transitions like morphs, transformation, and 'the door'"). The first eight words (axes, mount, spiral, suck, cut, dip, card, hold) were written from memory and the record refused them: the door, the snap, the throw-then-zoom and throw-then-push pair, park and un-park, the recast, the rescale, the compare melt, the morph, the remake and the object that becomes the chart had no name here and so no skeleton. EVERY word below carries TWO citations the test opens and greps: record= a line of CAPABILITIES.md or OPERATOR-RULINGS.md that marks the mechanism LIVE or WIRED, and cut= the line of a REAL shot table on disk that plays it. A word with no citation is refused. M46 refuses the same skeleton on two consecutive beats and WARNs over the approved maximum share (content/video_engine/effects/skeletons/approved-mix.json, MEASURED).

oneOf.title: the page enters ON ITS AXES
oneOf.description: The charcoal page lands with its ground, ruled line, title, labels and axes already drawn and the chart draws from the first frame - the open's own signature (E99 s67 Apply 6: the open STARTS ON THE CHART). record=docs/portable/OPERATOR-RULINGS.md:3252 cut=content/video_engine/projects/systems-and-blowups/memory-trades-the-calendar/build_short.py:138

oneOf.title: the page MOUNTS over the world that was there
oneOf.description: No roll-out and no savor: the cream is the ground at once, the soak opens on the first frame and runs mount_s, then ink then punch then build; the mount IS the transition, so nothing dips into it. record=docs/content-video-engine/CAPABILITIES.md:64 cut=content/video_engine/projects/systems-and-blowups/tokyo-tea-break/build_short.py:285

oneOf.title: the page RETURNS by the spiral, unwound from its point
oneOf.description: The page vortex run backwards: a page already drawn comes back by unwinding from the point it was sucked into, never drawn like new (E40 s4; E56 - the ring's one use). record=docs/content-video-engine/CAPABILITIES.md:57 cut=content/video_engine/projects/systems-and-blowups/tokyo-tea-break/build_short.py:338

oneOf.title: the thrown chart CARD becomes the page
oneOf.description: enter=snap=<dock>: the page grows from the landed card's own rectangle to the stage over SNAP_S 0.45 with a velocity-envelope blur and a whoosh - the card the viewer already read IS the world now. record=docs/content-video-engine/CAPABILITIES.md:76 cut=content/video_engine/projects/systems-and-blowups/tokyo-tea-break/build_short.py:416-420

oneOf.title: a full chart card is THROWN, then ZOOMS up to the whole stage
oneOf.description: The card-becomes-the-chart pair, both halves on one beat: the page's own card is thrown onto the standing world on the stop-action throw a second early, and the page then snaps up out of it. A thrown full-page card never floats over the plate - it zooms, or it pushes. record=docs/content-video-engine/CAPABILITIES.md:76 cut=content/video_engine/projects/systems-and-blowups/japan-tariff-trick/build_short.py:281-285

oneOf.title: a full chart card is THROWN, then the CAMERA pushes to it
oneOf.description: The same pair by the camera arrival: the card lands on the previous scene and over 0.45 s the camera zooms the outgoing world and the card together until the card's box fills the stage - the eye goes to the card instead of the card growing. record=docs/content-video-engine/CAPABILITIES.md:84 cut=content/video_engine/projects/systems-and-blowups/tokyo-tea-break/build_short.py:403-420

oneOf.title: the landed card swings OPEN onto the world beneath it
oneOf.description: THE EVIDENCE DOOR: a card that landed flat swings open on a hinge edge through the page plane's own projection until it is edge-on, onto the world mounted beneath it - min-jerk over DOOR.S 0.9 s, ending at 180 minus atan(d/h) so its back never shows. record=docs/content-video-engine/CAPABILITIES.md:38 cut=content/video_engine/projects/systems-and-blowups/japan-tariff-trick/build_short_door.py:41-59

oneOf.title: the world COLLAPSES into a point and the next opens in its place
oneOf.description: The page (or the plate) is sucked into a stage point, spinning SUCK_TURN while it scales away - page to page with no cream between them, and never into a mount. record=docs/content-video-engine/CAPABILITIES.md:57 cut=content/video_engine/projects/systems-and-blowups/tokyo-tea-break/build_short.py:328

oneOf.title: the world CHANGES, and the dip says so
oneOf.description: E47's world-change transition, 0.47 s: the one transition that means the world itself changed - never a dock's, never into a mount. record=docs/content-video-engine/CAPABILITIES.md:70 cut=content/video_engine/projects/systems-and-blowups/japan-tariff-trick/build_short.py:289

oneOf.title: a straight CUT, chart to chart
oneOf.description: A cut cuts: the world that left is gone on the new scene's first frame and the arriving page is on its axes, never empty cream. record=docs/content-video-engine/CAPABILITIES.md:26 cut=content/video_engine/projects/systems-and-blowups/memory-trades-the-calendar/build_short.py:223-227

oneOf.title: EVIDENCE arrives over the standing world
oneOf.description: A dock: a still, a document or a cutout thrown or landed over the world, read at its reading box and parked in the page's own room (E45, E65) - an evidence still, never a full chart page (E99 s67 Apply 5). record=docs/content-video-engine/CAPABILITIES.md:87 cut=content/video_engine/projects/systems-and-blowups/tokyo-tea-break/build_short.py:291

oneOf.title: the page STAYS and hosts what arrives over it
oneOf.description: The page rolls out on the hook and holds: the clips stop being scenes and arrive as docks over it, and the page is the constant the beat is argued on. record=docs/content-video-engine/CAPABILITIES.md:69 cut=content/video_engine/projects/systems-and-blowups/tokyo-tea-break/build_short.py:221-222

oneOf.title: the chart's AXES retarget to the window the sentence is about
oneOf.description: chart_to {to: rescale, ymin?, ymax?, window?}: the compiler derives the target state from the page's own series and the axes travel to it on one clock - the sell-off the sentence is about standing at full width. record=docs/content-video-engine/CAPABILITIES.md:115 cut=content/video_engine/projects/systems-and-blowups/tokyo-tea-break/build_short.py:312-313

oneOf.title: the SAME data changes FORM on the page
oneOf.description: chart_to {to: recast, state} on a page whose plate id declares the state as ;then=<series>:<variant>: the line un-draws by history, each keyed datum carries its place to the top of its bar, the categories write under the bars and the AXES HAND OVER across the clock. E64: a chart re-writes itself, it never just cuts to a new one. record=docs/content-video-engine/CAPABILITIES.md:27 cut=content/video_engine/projects/systems-and-blowups/tokyo-tea-break/build_short.py:383

oneOf.title: the chart makes ROOM by one affine transform
oneOf.description: chart_to {to: park, scale, anchor}: the active chart shrinks toward a corner of its own box on the min-jerk clock and holds - one transform on the whole svg, every mark in place, so the next thing has room beside it. Never emitted at 9:16 (R26-172). record=docs/content-video-engine/CAPABILITIES.md:120 cut=content/video_engine/projects/systems-and-blowups/tokyo-tea-break/build_short.py:314

oneOf.title: the chart RE-TAKES centre stage
oneOf.description: The park to scale 1.0: as the cards leave, the chart grows back to full from the standing park and its result holds large under the sentence that turns (the operator: the chart should re-take center stage). record=docs/content-video-engine/CAPABILITIES.md:120 cut=content/video_engine/projects/systems-and-blowups/tokyo-tea-break/build_short.py:394

oneOf.title: the quoted metric MELTS into the number the viewer feels
oneOf.description: The compare verb's melt form - chart_to {to: compare, form: melt, then: splash}: the quoted figure sags, balls up and splashes into the comparator the sentence turns on (E76 / E99 s56). record=docs/content-video-engine/CAPABILITIES.md:28 cut=content/video_engine/projects/systems-and-blowups/memory-trades-the-calendar/build_short.py:217-218

oneOf.title: one LINE's area hands over to another's by ARAP
oneOf.description: chart_to {to: morph, state} between two LINE pages: the standing line un-draws by length while its area fills, the filled strip morphs into the target's area as the axes hand over, and the target builds on its own law. record=docs/content-video-engine/CAPABILITIES.md:118 cut=content/video_engine/scripts/proof_chart_transitions.py:81 NO APPROVED CUT CARRIES IT: the only realisation on disk is the P48 proof surface, so this word has NO SKELETON - the record names the mechanism and a skeleton is never invented (E99 s70).

oneOf.title: the WHOLE chart becomes the whole other chart on one clock
oneOf.description: The seventh verb, chart_to {to: remake, state}, admitted on a line to bars pair only: every series, datum, axis, label and the title transform together (E99 s34 - a morph must prove the WHOLE chart). record=docs/content-video-engine/CAPABILITIES.md:119 cut=content/video_engine/scripts/render_baseline.py:253 NO APPROVED CUT CARRIES IT: the only realisation on disk is the remake-line-to-bars proof surface, so this word has NO SKELETON.

oneOf.title: the OBJECT in the picture becomes the chart
oneOf.description: enter=morph on a ledger page whose world.morph.poly is a PLANTED element's own traced silhouette: the prop the sentence just named becomes the area under the series, the ground soaking out from it, and the chart builds on the shape it became. record=docs/content-video-engine/CAPABILITIES.md:121 cut=content/video_engine/projects/systems-and-blowups/tokyo-tea-break/build-p61-planted/build_planted.py:119-133 The table it is transcribed from is a PROOF BUILD on the Tokyo bed (P61 T3d; E99 s60 - a proof is a scene), not one of the three approved shorts.

time_hole.description: a second in the take's clock, or one of the time holes {t0} / {t1} with an optional offset ({t0}+0.5); the build resolves it from the beat plan

open_map.description: an OPEN map (typed values, no fixed keys) - the only place this schema does not close an object, because the compiler's own option vocabulary is not this file's to freeze

oneOf.description: a dock id template - the named holes the build fills: {page} (the beat's series id), {plate} (the beat's plate id), {dock} (the beat's evidence dock), {t0} / {t1} (the beat's start and end from BEAT-PLAN.jsonl)

id.description: the dock id template; may carry the {dock} or {page} hole

read_s.description: how long it reads centred before it parks (SPECIES-BY-SENTENCE row 13, the dock read->park)

park_s.description: the layout move to its slot in the page's own room (E65)

options.description: the dock's own opts (centre, read, card_aspect ...); never an episode fact

oneOf.description: a dock that reads then parks, written out

kind.description: the targeted species kind (punch, callout, focus_zoom, spotlight, squiggle, pull_back, plate_life, trace, steam ...) - PIPELINE.md stage 7's `validate_species` vocabulary

dur.description: seconds, or "hold" until the sentence has a reason to leave (E25 amended)

target.description: the target the species declares - OPEN beyond `kind` (a datum's index and series, a region's box); a pointing species with no declared target is a hard build error

options.description: the rest of the species dict, carried verbatim into the row's 7th element

species.description: a TEMPLATE species; a light is placed only on a sentence that POINTS and never before the page's build ends (E99 s67 Apply 1-2; `rules.light_after_build`)

start.description: the row's start - usually the hole {t0}

end.description: the row's end - usually the hole {t1}; the compiler checks `rules.plate_min_s` against the resolved pair

plate.description: the plate id template in PIPELINE.md stage 7's grammar: a page as ledger:{page}:<variant>[:<emphasize>[:<quiet_zone>]] with an entry suffix (axes | mount=<s> | spiral | snap=<dock> | built) and an optional :cut, or a plate as {plate};idle=drift;drift=35. Holes: the named holes the build fills: {page} (the beat's series id), {plate} (the beat's plate id), {dock} (the beat's evidence dock), {t0} / {t1} (the beat's start and end from BEAT-PLAN.jsonl)

oneOf.description: the Ken Burns triple (zoom, dx, dy)
no move - a page is STILL
a hole the build fills with a triple

ken.description: the row's 4th element; a page carries none, an alive FLAT plate carries a directional drift

docks.description: the row's 5th element - the evidence that arrives over the world; may be empty

oneOf.description: NO transition: the world under a page that MOUNTS over it hands over by the mount itself (E45 - the mount IS the roll-out), which is how the approved open writes its first row: `tokyo-tea-break/build_short.py:281-282`, a 6th element of None

exit.description: how the world leaves (build_scene_timeline_f.SCENE_EXITS): `dip` when the world CHANGES (E47), `suck` or `cut` page to page and never into a mount; a suffix carries its length or point (dip:<s>, suck:<x>,<y>) and may itself carry a hole

species.description: the row's optional 7th element - the targeted species this skeleton places

row.description: ONE template row of the kit's grammar; the build resolves the holes and `table.write_shot_table` writes the tuple

mount_at_or_after_s.description: a page whose number lands this many seconds or more after its entry gets mount=<s>, never built (E99 s67 Apply 3)

plate_min_s.description: no plate row is shorter than this (M44)

event_gap_max_s.description: the longest gap between two events inside the skeleton (M16)

light_after_build.description: a light is placed only after the page's build ends (gate_motion_density.PAGE_BUILD_END_S; E99 s67 Apply 1-2)

rules.description: the clocks this skeleton must satisfy; all four are stated in every file so a reader never has to remember a default

no_badge_rail_at_9_16.description: R26-171: no `badges` rail is emitted at 9:16

aspect_limits.description: what the skeleton may NOT emit in portrait; the rail's const is true - a skeleton that wants otherwise is not a skeleton. R26-172 ('no `chart_to park` at 9:16') stood here as a second const until the parent read the APPROVED portrait cut beside the base (2026-09-17): at 56.72 s the page parks small at the top and the cards take the room below. The ruling is WITHDRAWN and the key is gone - the park is how a page makes room for a card, in both aspects

id.description: the slug, and the file name (open-on-the-chart-axes.json)

shape.description: the beat shape this skeleton serves - the shapes P65's beat-shapes.json names. A free string HERE on purpose (the two files are written by different plans) and the TWO FILES MUST AGREE: a shape named here that beat-shapes.json does not name is a bug in one of them, caught by T2's test, never by this schema

acts.description: the sentence acts whose beats this skeleton may serve; `shapes.choose` reads them

source.description: path:line in an APPROVED table where this shape was played (tokyo-tea-break / japan-tariff-trick / memory-trades-the-calendar build_short.py); T2's test opens the file at the line and greps it for the mechanism claimed, as effects_catalog_check.check_anchors does for a card's `lives`

does.description: one sentence: what the viewer sees this beat DO

schema_version.description: optional, as a recipe file carries effect_recipes.v1
